methodological_rigor.justification: This is a phase I open-label, multi-part, multi-center trial (NCT03616587) with separate dose-escalation (part I, n=16) and dose-expansion (part J, n=13) cohorts evaluating camizestrant 75 mg + capivasertib 400 mg (4d on/3d off). DLT assessment in a 28-day window, CTCAE v4.03 grading, central ECG triplicates, and predefined PK sampling at C1D18 and C2D1 with within-participant comparisons are methodologically appropriate. ctDNA ESR1m and PIK3CA/AKT1/PTEN analyses are prespecified with defined assays and thresholds. Statistics are appropriately descriptive for a phase I trial (Clopper-Pearson CIs for ORR, Kaplan-Meier for PFS); however, small sample sizes (n=29) produce wide CIs for subgroup estimates (e.g., ORR 46.2% in PIK3CA-altered tumors has 95% CI 19.2-74.9%), and no multiplicity correction is applied to the many subgroup comparisons, limiting inferential weight.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The study directly addresses the clinically important question of whether camizestrant (a next-generation oral SERD with demonstrated superiority over fulvestrant) can replace fulvestrant in the approved capivasertib + fulvestrant regimen for HR+/HER2- advanced breast cancer. The encouraging CBR24 of 51.7% and median PFS of 8.3 months in a heavily pretreated population (median 2 prior lines, 89.7% prior CDK4/6i), combined with clean PK/safety data, provide a strong signal to advance to phase III. Design corresponds to an individual early-phase trial, LoE 2b.

reporting_quality.justification: CONSORT is the nearest applicable standard for this phase I interventional trial. Reporting is comprehensive: trial registration, ethics, objectives, eligibility, dose rationale, safety grading, PK methodology, efficacy definitions, participant disposition in supplementary figures, and detailed AE tables are all present. Minor limitations include incomplete reporting of DLT evaluability details across all dose levels and no explicit CONSORT checklist. No statement about patient-level data or code sharing is evident; most detail is proprietary.

novelty_literature.justification: This is the first clinical report of a next-generation oral SERD (camizestrant) combined with an AKT inhibitor (capivasertib), positioning toward replacing fulvestrant in the approved capivasertib backbone. Given recently reported superiority of camizestrant over fulvestrant (SERENA-2) and recent SERENA-6 results in ESR1m-emergent disease, the combination has clear translational momentum. The contribution is novel but builds directly on extensively characterized single agents.

writing_presentation.justification: Clear, well-structured manuscript with logical flow from rationale through trial design, baseline characteristics, safety, PK, and efficacy including ctDNA dynamics. Figures and tables are appropriate (Kaplan-Meier not shown but PFS reported; waterfall/vector plots for ESR1m dynamics). Discussion places findings in context of SERENA-2, SERENA-6, CAPItello-291, and acknowledges limitations (open-label, small size, PTEN loss detection limitation). Writing is concise and professional.

key_strengths: Well-conducted phase I trial (NCT03616587) with prespecified PK sampling demonstrating no clinically relevant drug-drug interaction between camizestrant 75 mg and capivasertib 400 mg
Clinically meaningful efficacy signal (ORR 37.0%, CBR24 51.7%, median PFS 8.3 months) in a heavily pretreated population with 89.7% prior CDK4/6i
Consistent safety profile aligned with each agent as monotherapy, with most AEs grade 1-2, only 2 DLTs (grade 3 rash), and no camizestrant discontinuations
Incorporation of ctDNA ESR1m dynamics showing >=50% VAF reduction in 92% of assessable participants, strengthening mechanistic interpretation
key_concerns: Small sample size (n=29 combined) with wide subgroup CIs limits precision of biomarker-stratified efficacy estimates
Open-label, non-randomized, single-arm design precludes causal comparison to capivasertib + fulvestrant
PTEN loss not fully detectable by the Guardant360/Resolution Bioscience assays used, likely underestimating PIK3CA/AKT1/PTEN-altered prevalence
No data/code sharing statement; proprietary sponsor-driven trial limits independent reproducibility
chief_reviewer.rationale: Methodologically solid phase I combination trial with a clinically compelling safety/efficacy package that advances a next-generation SERD into AKT inhibitor combinations, appropriate for a Tier 2 oncology journal (e.g., Annals of Oncology, Clinical Cancer Research) but short of Tier 1 given its early-phase, single-arm nature.
